text_post: From the standpoint of what would constitute legitimate research, Lisak's work is bogus junk science. He probably sent out a questionnaire full of trick questions to a population of men who like to fancy themselves as tough guys always trying to exaggerate in order to convince everyone they are tougher than they are. Such men are not rapists, it's just a style of expression they have, a social class thing.  However, he was molested as a kid, and not in a random way. What he is talking about is part of a culture, part of certain mafia cultures, where serial rape plus laws criminalizing certain kinds of sex plus systematic cover ups plus blackmail all acts as a kind of glue to keep certain cultures perpetuating certain problems, yet it also serves certain structural purposes.  You have serial rapists where it is all systemetized. They are groomed, as victims, when they are children. It is almost, you could say, a form of training. And part of that is, they become perpetrators of sorts, but part of the "training" involves systematic dissembling and covering things up so well, they'd NEVER show up as rapists on any study designed to detect serial rapists in the population.  It is a phenomenon that cannot be studied in ordinary ways. Yet David Lisak knows all about it from his experiences in childhood. What is he supposed to do? Just not talk about it at all simply because he can't talk about it other than in a way that is very misleading and leads to wrong headed policies with regard to rape maybe? Though, to be honest, corruption in the criminal justice system is so rampant, all of the horrific written changes they have made to certain laws don't actually make it THAT much worse than it already was, given selective enforcement and the role class, race, and money play in the system anyway.  You can complain about his research and how it was misused and propagated by feminists who have said and done all the wrong things. Shouldn't you consider it your job merely to clarify things or not LET them misuse it in the wrong way?
